facts.statement: The study was a cross-sectional analysis of 135 inpatients diagnosed with cerebral small vessel disease.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers used the Potter scale to grade the size of enlarged perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia and centrum semiovale.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Sleep quality was measured with the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index, and cognitive function was evaluated using an education-adjusted version of the Montreal Cognitive Assessment.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: A higher grade of enlarged perivascular spaces in the basal ganglia was correlated with worse sleep quality scores and lower cognitive test scores.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: For every one-grade increase in the severity of basal ganglia perivascular spaces, the adjusted cognitive score was 1.133 points lower.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: The statistical analysis found an indirect effect of -0.6208 when sleep quality was considered as the pathway between perivascular spaces and cognition.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: When the statistical order was reversed to treat sleep as the starting factor, the indirect effect through perivascular spaces was -0.0609.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Subjective sleep quality and the time it takes to fall asleep were associated with cognitive scores in basic models, but this association did not hold in extended models.
facts.subject: humans
